glossary.definition: A land unit delineated in terms of major climate parameters (rainfall, temperature, humidity) and water resource availability, suitable for a characteristic range of crops and cultivars.
A geographic unit carved out of an agro-climatic zone, modified by landform/physiography and soil conditions, having a characteristic Length of Growing Period (LGP) and ecological carrying capacity.

The continuous period in days during the year when rainfall exceeds 50% of Potential Evapotranspiration (P > 0.5 PET), plus the period required to deplete up to 100 mm of available soil moisture stored in the profile following the cessation of rain.
The maximum rate of water vapor loss from an extensive, closed, short-vegetation surface with unlimited water supply, reflecting the atmospheric evaporative demand.
A climatic indicator formulated by Thornthwaite and Mather, expressed as MI = (P - PET) / PET, used to categorize bioclimate from arid to perhumid.

Dark basalt-derived vertisol (black cotton soil) rich in montmorillonitic clay, characterized by high shrink-swell capacity, self-ploughing cracks during summer, and exceptional water-retentive capability.
Geomorphic divisions of the Indo-Gangetic alluvium: Khadar is younger, nutrient-replenished floodplain alluvium; Bhangar is older, elevated alluvium containing calcareous kankar nodules.
Traditional slash-and-burn agricultural cycle practiced on hill slopes of North-East India, resulting in accelerated soil erosion and deforestation when fallow cycles shorten.
glossary.source: Forest Survey of India / ICAR-RC NEH

glossary.definition: Open-field burning of paddy straw practiced predominantly in the Trans-Gangetic Plains (Zone 6) to quickly clear fields between kharif harvest and rabi wheat sowing.
Water-saving cultivation technique where pre-germinated paddy seeds are sown directly into unpuddled soil, conserving 20-30% irrigation water and eliminating nursery transplantation.

The official Government of India nomenclature designating nutri-cereals and millets (Jowar, Bajra, Ragi, Kodo, Kutki, Kangni), promoted for drought resilience, nutritional security, and low water footprints.
glossary.source: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, GoI (2023)
